topic: Aired up the tire and the low-pressure light is still on? Here's why it doesn't clear right away.

beats.vo: Aired up the tire and the low-pressure light is still on?
beats.visual: Macro shot of a tire pressure gauge dial, needle settling, pressed to a valve stem against a dark tire sidewall backdrop, static camera

beats.vo: Most systems don't clear the second you fill it — they need a short drive to recheck all four sensors.
beats.visual: Interior wide shot of a dashboard instrument cluster with the TPMS icon illuminated, static mounted camera, dim ambient cabin light

beats.vo: Give it a few minutes above around fifteen miles an hour. If it's still lit after that, double-check every tire actually got filled — not just the one that looked low.
beats.visual: Sequence of four macro valve-stem shots in a row implying all four corners, consistent studio lighting, static/locked pans between cuts

beats.vo: A light that stays on after a real drive may indicate a sensor issue, not just low pressure.
beats.visual: Close-up of a handheld diagnostic scanner plugged into an OBD port beneath a dash, screen glow soft-focus, static camera, no hand in frame

beats.vo: Worth checking if it lingers. Stop by and we'll take a look.
